Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Williams could miss consecutive games due to a knee injury, which would mark the second missed game of his young career. If the seventh-round rookie must miss another contest, Josh Fryar would be set to start Sunday's game at left tackle.

Carter will remain on IR for Week 10 and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams. The defensive tackle logged three consecutive limited practices after being designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday.

Gaines was set to start at center due to the absence of Hjalte Froholdt (concussion). With Gaines also unable to suit up due to an ankle injury, Hayden Conner will make his first career start at center against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett.

Froholdt appeared on the Cardinals' injury report Wednesday with a concussion and has not progressed in his recovery. Both Froholdt and backup center Jon Gaines (ankle) will not suit up for Sunday's game, leaving third-string right guard Hayden Conner as the starting center for Sunday's game.

Wingard was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice but ended Week 10 prep with consecutive DNPs. The free safety remains questionable despite multiple absences, but if he is inactive come game time, Kitan Crawford is set to start in his place.

The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.
With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.

Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Deablo was cleared to return for Week 9 against the Bengals after missing the Falcons' two prior games due to a forearm injury. He may have aggravated the injury against Cincinnati, and he logged consecutive DNPs to end Week 10 prep. He hasn't been ruled out yet, but assuming Deablo doesn't play, Harold Perkins would be the top candidate to start alongside Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker.

Branch missed a Week 9 loss to the Bengals and didn't practice this week. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair took on extra snaps in Branch's absence last week. The good news for Branch is that Atlanta has a bye coming up after Sunday's game.

Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.

Hawkins missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, he likely has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to suit up Monday night against the Chargers. If Hawkins can't play, K'Von Wallace should continue to see more snaps.

Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Brown overcame a back injury to suit up for the Bills' Week 9 win over the Vikings on Monday. The right tackle picked up an ankle injury during the contest and ended Week 10 prep with consecutive DNPs. If the right tackle does not suit up for Sunday's game, Tylan Grable would be set to return to a starting role against the Jets.

Benford injured his wrist during the Bills' Monday night win over the Vikings, though he returned to the contest after sustaining the injury. The cornerback started Week 10 prep with consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. Benford will likely suit up for Sunday's contest to start in a secondary that should be bolstered by the trade-deadline acquisition of Amani Hooker.

Shavers was a full participant in all three practices during Week 10 prep, but he would need to be activated from the reserve/PUP list in order to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Shavers is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he suffered during the Bills' 27-24 win over the Jaguars in the 2025 AFC wild-card round in January.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Jackson was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, which cleared him to practice during Week 10 prep. He logged a trio of limited practices, but the doubtful tag indicates that the veteran defensive back will spend at least one more week on IR. If he's not cleared to play in Week 10, then Jackson's next opportunity to play would be Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in Week 8, which prevented him from playing in Week 9 against the Broncos. He was a full participant in practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but his reps were limited during Friday's session, which may have been for maintenance reasons. Regardless, Lee's official status for Sunday's NFC South tilt may not be officially known until the Panthers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Mike Jackson (groin, IR) is listed as doubtful, so it's unclear who the Panthers will turn to at outside cornerback opposite Malcolm DeWalt if Lee is unable to play.

Legette is trending toward a return from injured reserve after the Panthers listed him as a full practice participant all week. They'll need to activate him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Legette on the active roster for Sunday's NFC South showdown. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver before the injury, often running clear-out routes while Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker dominated the targets. John Metchie and Brycen Tremayne took on more snaps in Legette's absence over the past month-plus.

Brooks remains on injured reserve and isn't likely to be activated by the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday. He was listed as a full practice participant at the beginning of the week, but coach Dave Canales revealed Friday that there was a reporting error with Brooks and CB Mike Jackson (groin), both of whom should have been listed as limited. Both were then listed as limited Thursday and Friday, with 'doubtful' designations for Sunday's game. Brooks appears on track to return for Week 11 or 12, at which point he could take a few touches away from Chuba Hubbard.

Okereke was estimated as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he remained sidelined for Thursday's full-speed practice. Barring a return to practice Friday, Okereke could be in line for a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Saints after he racked up 49 tackles (31 solo) through his first seven games with the Panthers.

Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.
With Stevenson sidelined and Malik Muhammad (toe) inactive, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips will take on more defensive snaps alongside Jaylon Phillips and Kyler Gordon at cornerback for the Bears.

Muhammad was expected to be able to return to action in Week 9, but the cornerback will now be forced to miss a second straight game while nursing a toe injury he suffered in Week 7. In his absence, Josh Blackwell is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities at cornerback behind starters Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson versus the Buccaneers.

Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.
Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Dugger has not been cleared to return to practice since suffering a quadriceps injury in Week 7. The reserve strong safety will miss a third consecutive game due to the injury, leaving Russ Yeast and PJ Jules to back up starter Jordan Battle.
Iosivas returned to practice Thursday and was a full participant both Thursday and Friday. He should be ready for Week 11, at which point he'll likely take the No. 3 WR job back from Dohnte Meyers.

Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.

Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Burton injured his calf during the Browns' Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints. He was cleared to return in that contest but was unable to practice during Week 10 prep. The Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man active roster nor the practice squad, so they may have to utilize tight end Blake Whiteheart as a backfield blocker. Burton will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Browns' Week 11 bye, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Hickman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he recorded nine tackles (four solo) and two pass defenses. He was unable to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep, and his absence means rookie second-rounder Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will likely start alongside Grant Delpit at safety, with Daniel Thomas and Donovan McMillon both providing depth at the position. The Browns are on a bye for Week 11, so Hickman will have additional time to progress through the five-step concussion protocol before Week 12 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

With that in mind, coach Todd Monken noted Friday that Boston "moved around pretty good...it's trending in the right way." It's worth noting, however, that Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer relays that Boston left the team's locker room in a walking boot, but it's possible that's simply a precautionary measure. Either way, the wideout's Week 10 status will be known prior to the first batch of games Sunday, with the Browns kicking off at 1:00 pm ET. Assuming he's available this weekend, Boston and fellow rookie KC Concepcion would be in line to lead Cleveland's WR corps versus Houston, with Jerry Jeudy also in the mix.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Ezeiruaku suffered an ankle injury during the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts in Week 9. He was not cleared to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep, and his absence means Von Miller, James Houston and Marist Liufau are all in line for more defensive snaps Sunday. Ezeiruaku's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Porter was unable to play against the Colts in Week 9 due to an ankle injury, and he posted a DNP-DNP-LP practice log for Week 10 prep. DaRon Bland (ankle) is also listed as questionable, and the next options available for outside cornerback are Cobie Durant, Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel.

Bland first appeared on Friday's practice report as a limited participant, which indicates that he injured his ankle during that session. That's not a good sign for Bland heading into the weekend, and the Cowboys could be without both of their starting outside cornerbacks depending on the status of Joey Porter (ankle), who is also listed as questionable. Cobie Durant, Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel are the top candidates to start at outside cornerback if one or both of Bland or Porter were to miss time.

Mingo was held out of practice all week while recovering from foot and ankle injuries that he picked up during the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts in Week 9. In his absence, KaVontae Turpin -- who is returning from a three-game absence due to a rib injury -- and Camden Brown are both in line for a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Mingo's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 22.

The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

Locke suffered a concussion in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. While he was cleared to play in Week 9 against the Colts, he suffered another concussion. Now, Locke will miss at least one game, though the team will presumably be overly cautious before allowing him to get back on the field, meaning Markquese Bell may be in line for more snaps.

At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

Denver Broncos.longComment: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.
Moss has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Jahdae Barron will likely finish the game at outside cornerback for the Broncos.

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Vaki played through the same injury last week, taking five touches for 21 yards in a 19-9 win over the Dolphins. He didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday this week, but a return to practice Friday puts him on track to avoid the inactive list ahead of Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. If Vaki doesn't end up playing, Jacob Saylors will step into the No. 2 RB role behind workhorse Jahmyr Gibbs.

St. Brown played through the same injury (and same 'questionable' tag) last week, catching eight passes for 86 yards on a team-high 10 targets in Detroit's 19-9 win over Miami. He'll likely play again, but fantasy managers will want to make sure of it when the Lions release their inactive list at 8:00 a.m. ET on Sunday. St. Brown has been a limited participant in every practice since first injuring his ribs in a Week 8 win over Minnesota.

Mays will sit out a second straight contest as he continues to recover from the high-ankle sprain he suffered in Week 8 versus the Vikings. In his absence, Juice Scruggs figures to make another start at center in Week 10.

Reed did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a hip injury suffered late in Week 8. Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw could see extended playing time for the second straight week in Reed's stead. Reed has 42 tackles (29 solo) and seven pass deflections, including one interception, in seven regular-season games.

Joseph was a full participant in practice Thursday, but it appears the Lions are taking a cautious approach to his return. The 25-year-old has one more chance to return from the reserve/PUP list in Week 11 before he becomes ineligible for the remainder of the season.

Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Zeitler was held out of Friday's practice while tending to ankle and triceps injuries. He signed with the Packers in late September but has not started in each of his four appearances with Green Bay. His absence would weaken the Packers' depth on the offensive line.

Glover didn't play against the Patriots in Week 9 due to a knee injury. He was limited in practice in all three Week 10 sessions, but if he cannot play Sunday, then Laken Tomlinson will likely start at right guard.

Rhyan will miss a third consecutive game due to an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Josh Williams is expected to start at center in Rhyan's absence.

Van Ness logged a limited practice Friday after consecutive DNPs to start Week 10 prep. The linebacker could suit up for Sunday's game if his back feels better by game day. If Van Ness ends up inactive for the NFC North showdown, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton are set to split snaps across from Barryn Sorrell.

Bullard was a non-participant in consecutive sessions to start Week 10 prep before upgrading to limited in Friday's practice. The slot cornerback now has a chance to suit up for Sunday's game, but with just one practice under his belt, it is more likely that Kamal Hadden takes over the role against the Vikings.

Franklin was a non-participant throughout the Packers' Week 10 prep, but the linebacker has not yet been officially ruled out ahead of Sunday's divisional contest. If Franklin is inactive come game time, Isaiah McDuffie is in line to take over as the starting inside linebacker opposite Ty'Ron Hopper.

Whyle missed all of the Packers' Week 10 prep due to a concussion. The tight end remains in the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest, leaving Mark Redman and Jonnu Smith as the depth options behind Tucker Kraft.

Moore has remained on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 5. The wide receiver logged limited practice sessions throughout Week 10 prep but likely will not be elevated for Sunday's contest, as the Packers are set to allocate any additional roster space to the running back position in Josh Jacobs' (finger) absence.

Brooks logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 10 prep as he works his way back from an ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 that landed the running back on IR. With Josh Jacobs (finger) ruled out for Sunday's divisional contest, Brooks could be activated ahead of Sunday's game to play alongside MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson.

McKinney was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a foot injury. His late addition to the practice report isn't a good sign, and McKinney is now in jeopardy of missing his first game due to injury since the 2022 campaign, when he was a member of the Giants. Kitan Oladapo and Kamal Hadden would be the top candidates to start at safety alongside Evan Williams if McKinney is unable to play Sunday.

Parsons now has put together back-to-back weeks of limited sessions as he inches closer to his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. With a Week 11 bye on tap, he'll have a bit more time to get healthy before the Packers' Week 12 road matchup with the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which coincides with his 21-day practice window coming to a close.

Brinson suffered a calf injury during the preseason that forced him to miss the Packers' first three regular-season games before he was ultimately sent to injured reserve in early October. LaFleur also said Thursday that Brinson is recovering from a groin surgery, which could be a factor in his extended absence. Until he comes back from IR, Anthony Campbell figures to continue to see increased reps on the defensive line in his stead.

Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and is in line to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are currently available to handle Green Bay's backfield duties while Jacobs is sidelined, plus Chris Brooks (ankle) is a candidate to return from IR as soon as this weekend.

Houston Texans.longComment: Rutledge did not participate in any Week 10 prep for the Texans. The rookie offensive guard will not suit up for Sunday's contest, leaving Wyatt Teller (illness) or Evan Brown to start at left guard in a game with massive potential playoff implications for both the Texans and the Browns.

Anderson was added to Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. He was held out of Friday's session, but that may have been as a precautionary measure to prevent an injury aggravation. Danielle Hunter (hamstring) has already been ruled out, so the Texans would have to rely on Jadeveon Clowney, Dominique Robinson and Sabastian Harsh as the top defensive ends if Anderson cannot play Sunday.

Hunter popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was unable to practice Friday, and the injury is severe enough for him to miss his first game of the 2026 regular season. The Texans could also be without fellow star edge rusher Will Anderson (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game despite also sitting out of Friday's practice. Jadeveon Clowney, Dominique Robinson and Sabastian Harsh will all see more defensive snaps in the absence of Hunter, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against Indianapolis on Thursday.

Jordan was unable to practice all week while tending to a finger injury, and his absence Sunday means Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover are all in line for more snaps on offense behind starting tight end Dalton Schultz. Jordan's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

Al-Shaair was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury and a personal matter, although it's unclear which issue is the bigger reason why the veteran linebacker will be sidelined for Sunday's road contest. Wade Woodaz and Jake Hummel (groin) -- the latter of whom is on injured reserve -- are the top candidates to start alongside Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hansen at linebacker. Al-Shaair's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

Montgomery returned to practice Thursday after missing a month, and he upgraded from limited participation to full for Friday's practice. It's still not clear he'll be active ahead of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday, so Marks could be tasked with a heavy workload for a fifth straight game. If Montgomery does return, he'll likely share work with Marks, making it difficult to trust either Houston RB in fantasy lineups.

Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Hummel was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and it was encouraging to see him back on the field after recovering from groin surgery. The Texans face the Browns on Sunday, but Hummel would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for that contest.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Travis did not participate in Week 10 prep as he continues to recover from a knee injury he suffered during the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Jaguars. Luke Tenuta is set to start at right tackle for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

Carlies exited the first half of the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys with a neck injury and did not return to the contest. The linebacker was unable to practice at all during Week 10 prep and has not progressed in his recovery. Austin Ajiake is set to be the backup middle linebacker to CJ Allen in Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

Tillery was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury before being sidelined for both Thursday and Friday. Tim Smith and Kevin Givens are in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Tillery, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

Rhodes was held out of practice all week due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday. The Colts will likely elevate Jacob Bobenmoyer from the practice squad to serve as the team's long snapper for Sunday's contest.

Mallory was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. His late addition isn't a great sign heading into the weekend, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) already ruled out, the Colts would turn to both Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown to step into larger roles behind Tyler Warren if Mallory is also sidelined.

Davis-Gaither is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he likely picked up during the Colts' Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. His next chance to play is Thursday against the Texans, although Davis-Gaither was unable to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Jaylon Carlies (neck) is ruled out for Sunday's contest, so Austin Ajiake figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Bryce Boettcher and CJ Allen at linebacker, with Tahj Chambers providing depth at the position.

Alie-Cox suffered a groin injury during the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, and that injury prevented the veteran tight end from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Will Mallory (hamstring) is listed as questionable, so the Colts may have to rely more heavily on Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown to provide depth at tight end behind starter Tyler Warren for Sunday's contest. Alie-Cox's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

Key hasn't played since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Commanders. Now, after five weeks, the 30-year-old may begin practicing. He will likely need to string together multiple positive practices for a chance to play in Week 10.

"We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Moore suffered an ankle injury in the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets. The right tackle will not suit up for Sunday's game due to the injury, leaving Joshua Ezeudu to start against the Falcons.

Woods will miss consecutive games due to a neck injury he sustained early in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is progressing in his recovery, but it remains unclear when he will return to the field.

Ott popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was also limited in Friday's session, and with Kenneth Walker (groin) also questionable, the Chiefs enter the weekend with Emmett Johnson as the only healthy running back on the 53-man roster. Nate Carter is the only running back on Kansas City's practice squad and would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of both Ott and Walker.

Delane has missed the Chiefs' last two games while recovering from a shoulder injury. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 10 prep, but that evidently wasn't enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's road game. Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace would continue to operate in elevated roles in the secondary if Delane is not cleared to return.

Walker was added to the Chiefs' Week 10 injury report due to groin tightness that kept him from practicing Friday. Now that he's carrying an official 'questionable' designation heading into the weekend, the running back's status will need to be tracked as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. In the event that Walker -- who is averaging a robust 109.0 rushing yards per game and has scored 11 total TDs through eight contests -- is made inactive for the contest,  Emmett Johnson would be in line to handle the bulk of the team's carries versus Atlanta.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Booker remains questionable despite upgrading to a full participant in Friday's practice session. The defensive lineman is likely a game-time decision, and if he is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, JJ Pegues will likely see more defensive snaps.

Thornton was unable to practice Friday due to a back injury that he likely picked up at some point during Week 10 prep. His late addition to the injury report isn't a good sign for his availability Sunday, although he has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026, mostly due to a hamstring injury that landed him on injured reserve in late August.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Pipkins has been on injured reserve since late September due to a knee injury. He's opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP's, so it's unlikely that he'll be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.

Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

Leonard was upgraded to full participation for Friday's session after being limited Thursday. The cornerback has not yet officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, but a return to full practice means he should be all set to suit up for the Chargers' Monday night contest against the Ravens.

It's a new injury for Mitchell, who also was limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

McConkey -- who dealt with back spasms last Sunday and as a result didn't log any snaps in the 0-8 Chargers' loss to the Texans, has now missed back-to-back practices, so what he's able to do Saturday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Monday night's game against the Ravens. If McConkey is unavailable for the contest, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would be in line to head Los Angeles' WR corps, as they did versus Houston.
Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders. It appears he will remain on the shelf for Monday's game versus the Ravens unless he shows signs of progress in the next few days.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Avila suffered a hamstring injury against the Commanders in Week 9, and it's not clear if a stint on injured reserve is necessary for the fourth-year offensive guard. If he's not placed on IR, then his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

McDuffie was a DNP for both Wednesday and Thursday before logging a limited session Friday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag, but head coach Sean McVay relayed optimism Friday that McDuffie would be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt, per Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register. Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace and Cam Lampkin would all be in line for larger roles in the secondary if McDuffie cannot play or operates under a snap count.

Curl opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to a toe injury before logging a limited session Friday, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. That was enough for Curl to get the questionable tag for Sunday's game, although McVay's comments suggest that the veteran safety is on the probable side to play in Week 10. If Curl cannot play or operates under a snap count, then Jaylen McCollough would be in line for a larger role in the Rams' secondary.

Allen put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log during Week 10 prep while managing an oblique injury, which he likely picked up during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders. If he cannot play Sunday, then Max Klare would operate as the team's TE3 behind Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Allen's status may not be officially known until about 90 minutes before the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Rams announce their list of inactive players.

Garrett made his presence felt in his return to the lineup this past Sunday at Washington, sacking Commanders QB Jayden Daniels three times, but the Rams capped his practice reps this week due to a listed knee injury. McVay's comments indicate Garrett isn't in danger of sitting out Week 10, but the pass rusher's status nonetheless will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

With this transaction officially in the books, Nacua will be required to miss at least the next four games due to the PCL and MCL sprains and turf-toe injury that he sustained near the end of this past Sunday's win at Washington. During the initial stage of Nacua's absence, the Rams will lean on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wide receiver until Davante Adams (hamstring) is ready to return from injured reserve.

In that scenario, Adams could back in action as soon as Week 12 following the Rams' bye week. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is destined to miss multiple weeks, which, for the time being leaves Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Danielsand Xavier Smith as the healthy WRs on the team's active roster.

This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Brewer suffered a concussion during Week 10 prep and will not play in Sunday's contest. The center has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact activities.

Wayne popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quadriceps injury, which prevented him from suiting up for Friday's session. He won't be available for Sunday's contest, and it appears the Dolphins will also be without rookie third-rounder Chris Bell (knee), who is listed as doubtful. Wayne's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Bell was a limited practice participant Wednesday before sitting out Thursday and Friday. The injury is to his surgically repaired knee, but coach Jeff Hafley was quick to specify that the current issue isn't related to the ACL repair from last year. It sounds like Bell could be back within a week or two. For now, No. 4 receiver Kevin Coleman figures to get more playing time.

Baker has been on Miami's PUP list since August, but it looks like he's making progress toward returning to game action soon. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which the Dolphins can activate him before they'd be required to keep him inactive for the rest of the campaign.

With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Ingram-Dawkins injured his ankle during the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday. The injury prevented from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep, so he won't be available for Sunday's NFC North showdown. Elijah Williams and Domonique Orange are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Ingram-Dawkins, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Metellus was a late addition to the Vikings' practice report, with the veteran safety popping up as a limited participant for Friday's session due to a shoulder injury. His late addition is concerning for the Vikings, and if Metellus cannot play Sunday, then Theo Jackson and Jay Ward would be the top candidates to start at safety alongside Harrison Smith.

Cashman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday. He was cleared to participate in Friday's practice in a no-contact jersey, per Goessling, but Cashman will not clear league protocol in time for Sunday's NFC North tilt. Ivan Pace will be the next man up at inside linebacker next to Eric Wilson due to the absence of Cashman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Jennings opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP listings due to a calf injury and now will miss his second contest of the campaign. With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

After head coach Kevin O'Connell called Murray week-to-week due to his Grade 2 hamstring injury Wednesday, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com, the quarterback's second straight absence as a result was expected. O'Connell announced recent acquisition Kirk Cousins as the Vikings' starting QB for Week 10, and that should hold even after Murray gets back to full health.

Addison didn't make an appearance on the Vikings' Week 10 injury report until Friday, and now his status is up in the air ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. If he's able to suit up this weekend, he'll be on the receiving end of passes from new starting QB Kirk Cousins.

Hockenson wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep due to wrist and chest injuries and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. In Hockenson's absence, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew will step into more prominent roles in the Vikings offense, while Devin Culp will be a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad.

Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

New England Patriots.longComment: Schooler was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury he sustained during the Patriots' Week 9 loss to the Packers. He ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and his absence would deplete the Patriots' depth both in the secondary and on special teams. Starting safety Kevin Byard (chest) is also listed as questionable despite logging a full practice Friday.

Woods was unable to play against the Packers in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. He opened Week 10 prep with consecutive limited practices before participating in full Friday, but his official status for Sunday's contest may not be known until New England announces its list of inactive players about 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. Carlton Davis (knee) did not travel with the team to Germany, and if Woods is not cleared to play Sunday, then Channing Canada and Karon Prunty would be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

Byard opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to fade the injury tag for Sunday's international game, so the veteran safety's status may not be officially known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. Jaylen Reed would be the top candidate to start alongside Craig Woodson at safety if Byard is not cleared to play against Detroit.

Despite a report earlier in the week indicating that Stevenson would likely miss some time, the running back's ability to log limited practices both Thursday and Friday gives him a chance to play this weekend. With a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled, those considering Stevenson or A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) in Week 10 fantasy lineups will have the duo's statuses clarified before the first wave of games Sunday. Moreover, there's a pretty good chance that NFL insiders such as Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network and Adam Schefter of ESPN will provide some updates on New England's injury situation either late Saturday or early Sunday. If the team ends up holding Stevenson out ahead of a Week 11 bye, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined.

The same applies to RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), with coach Mike Vrabel having said "pretty good" when asked before Friday's practice about his view on how the duo was progressing toward playing this weekend. Fortunately for those considering Brown (who was listed as limited at practice Wednesday through Friday) in Week 10 fantasy lineups, his status will be known before the first wave of games Sunday, with a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled.

On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings representing a possible practice squad elevation.

Brown tweaked his knee against the Packers in Week 9, and the injury is severe enough for him to not travel with the team to Munich. In his absence, Walter Rouse is expected to serve as the Patriots' starter at left guard. Since the Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, Brown's next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
The fullback hasn't played since Week 4. He's logged 58 snaps on offense and another 39 on special teams across four appearances this season.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: McCoy is expected to miss multiple games while tending to a biceps injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Browns. Cesar Ruiz is expected to serve as the Saints' starting center for as long as McCoy is sidelined.

The rookie second-rounder was held out of practice both Thursday and Friday due to a knee injury, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 22. Khristian Boyd, Colby Wooden and Tyree Wilson are all in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Miller's absence.

Fuaga is dealing with a knee sprain that he sustained during Thursday's practice, per Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com. However, head coach Kellen Moore indicated Friday that he doesn't expect Fuaga to be sidelined long term, as reported by Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio. Mason Murphy and Asim Richards are the top candidates to start at right tackle in Fuaga's absence.

Emerson's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a shin injury. He was able to play through the injury in Week 9 against the Browns, and he finished that contest with two solo tackles in a 23-22 overtime win for the Saints. Second-year pro Quincy Riley would likely be the next man up at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry if Emerson is unable to play Sunday.

Donaldson will miss a third straight game, while Travis Etienne (hamstring) has a chance to return from injured reserve. With Etienne listed as questionable, Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara could have significant roles. Donaldson mostly has played in obvious passing situations this year, often staying in as a blocker.

Etienne remains on injured reserve and officially is listed as questionable for Week 10, per Ross Jackson of WWL-TV. After the Saints designated Etienne for return from IR on Wednesday, he opened the week with back-to-back limited sessions before logging a full practice Friday, but the team still will need to activate him by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. With CJ Donaldson (shoulder) ruled out, Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime will be the other RBs to vie with for touches if Etienne is able to suit up this weekend.

New York Giants.longComment: Pinnock exited the game early in the third quarter with a back injury, and his status for the rest of the game is uncertain. In his absence, Tyler Nubin will be thrust into a more prominent role in New York's secondary.

Harrison was limited at practice throughout the week and has since been ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with the Commanders. The 28-year-old has played sparingly on defense during the 2026 campaign, though his absence will be felt on special teams. Harrison's next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 11 versus Jacksonville.

New York Jets.longComment: A back injury prevented Wright from playing against the Chiefs in Week 9. He logged a full practice Friday, but it wasn't enough for him to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's AFC East tilt. His absence would mean less depth in the Jets' secondary and one less contributor on special teams.

Phillips missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep while recovering from an ankle injury. He was a full participant in Friday's session, so he may be considered more toward the probable side of playing Sunday. If Phillips cannot play, then both Jack Heflin and Payton Page would be in line for more rotational snaps on the interior defensive line behind Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson.

Ossai has a chance to return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury after stringing together a trio of limited practices during Week 10 prep. His return would give the Jets additional depth at defensive end behind Kingsley Enagbare and David Bailey.

Brownlee was unable to practice Thursday due to an illness, but he was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity. He'll have the weekend to shake off his illness, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Jets announce their list of inactive players. Rookie second-rounder D'Angelo Ponds would have a larger role in the Jets' secondary if Brownlee is not cleared to play.

Wallace was held out of practice all week while recovering from a groin injury, which will prevent him from playing in a second consecutive game. Most of his snaps this season have come on special teams, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at linebacker for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Wallace's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

The same goes for top receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) as well as Adonai Mitchell (knee). The trio's full practice participation Friday suggests that all three players will be available Sunday, but their statuses will nonetheless need to be confirmed ahead of Week 10 action due to their official game designations. Fortunately for fantasy managers who have shares in any of the Jets' top three WRs, the team kicks off at 1:00 pm ET on Sunday.

Fellow wideouts Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper (ankle) also are listed as questionable despite being full practice participants Friday. Both figure to play, as does Mitchell, who finished without a catch on seven targets (two drops) in last week's loss to the Chiefs -- one week after catching seven passes for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. Wilson's likely return to the lineup means Mitchell isn't assured of similar volume moving forward.

Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.

Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Harmon missed the Steelers' four games prior to the Week 9 bye while on injured reserve due to a foot injury. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and ended Week 10 prep with a full session Friday, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown. Harmon's return would bolster the Steelers' defensive line behind Yahya Black, Keeanu Benton and Cameron Heyward.

Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Williams downgraded to a non-participant in Friday's practice after upgrading to a limited participant for Thursday's session. The left tackle was likely taking vet rest ahead of Sunday's game as he prepares to suit up through his shoulder injury against the Cowboys.

Green missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep due to a back injury that he sustained during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9. He was limited in Friday's practice, and if he cannot play Sunday, then rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Nate Hobbs (groin, IR) would be candidates for elevated roles in the secondary.

Lenoir injured his foot during the 49ers' Week 9 win over the Raiders. He was able to log a limited practice Friday after being sidelined both Wednesday and Thursday, and that limited session was enough for him to draw the questionable tag. Rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Ashtyn Davis would be in line for more snaps in the secondary if Lenoir is unable to play Sunday.

Greenlaw tweaked his knee during Thursday's practice, but he was cleared to participate in Friday's session in a limited capacity, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com. Garret Wallow, Tatum Bethune and Luke Gifford would all be in line to start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger if Greenlaw is unable to play Sunday.

Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.

The 49ers opened West's 21-day practice window Wednesday, and he was limited in his return to on-field practice. He landed on injured reserve in late September due to a knee injury, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys.

Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season. The fourth-round rookie finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 15 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, a defensed pass, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery (which he returned for a touchdown) over eight contests. San Francisco's recent acquisition of DeForest Buckner softens the blow of losing Halton a bit.

In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Nelson's absence doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he underwent a minor procedure on his injured knee Monday. He's currently considered week-to-week, and with the Seahawks on a bye for Week 11, Nelson could return for Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Grey Zabel will likely start at left guard Sunday in Nelson's stead.

Cross logged a limited practice Thursday before being held out of Friday's session, and he'll end up missing a third consecutive game due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered against the Chiefs in Week 7. The Seahawks are on a bye for Week 11, so Cross will extra time to recover before Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Josh Jones will likely start at left tackle in Cross's absence.

Williams will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a shoulder injury, which prevented him from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Mike Morris and Rylie Mills will operate in expanded roles on defense in the absence of Williams, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29, since the Seahawks are on a bye for Week 11.

Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Winfield sustained an ankle injury late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. With Winfield unavailable, Ifeatu Melifonwu will continue to operate as one of Tampa Bay's primary safeties versus Chicago.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Townsend didn't play in Week 8 due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 7 against the Browns. He had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 9 bye and was a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday. However, Townsend was held out of Friday's session, and a right Achilles injury was added to his designation. Thomas Morstead will likely be called up from the practice squad to punt for the Titans on Sunday.

Skoronski injured his hamstring against the Bengals in Week 8, and the Week 9 bye did not provide enough recovery time to return for Week 10. Garrett Dellinger filled in for left guard following Skoronski's injury, although head coach Robert Saleh told reporters Friday that he has not committed to a starting LG for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Skoronski's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Barton was unable to practice during Week 10 prep while in the league's concussion protocol, which he may have entered following the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. Rookie second-rounder Anthony Hill (neck) has also been ruled out, which leaves Dorian Mausi and Mohamoud Diabate as the likely candidates to start at linebacker alongside Cedric Gray for Sunday's contest. Barton's next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22, although he would have to return to practice in at least a limited capacity to demonstrate that he's progressing in the league's five-step protocol.

Hill may have injured his neck during the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. The Week 9 bye provided the rookie second-rounder extra time to rest, but he was not cleared to practice during Week 10 prep and will miss his first game of the regular season. Cody Barton (concussion) has also been ruled out, so Mohamoud Diabate and Dorian Mausi both figure to start alongside Cedric Gray at linebacker for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Hill's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22.

A return to action after missing two games would hurt Tony Pollard's workload projection, though Pollard would still be in line for most of the carries. There have also been hints of rookie Nicholas Singleton getting playing time in the second half of the season, leaving Spears without much of a path to mainstream fantasy value.

There was previously some optimism that Tate -- who last played in Week 7 -- would be able to return after the Titans' Week 9 bye, but the wideout's absence will continue at least until Nov. 22 against the Cowboys, a contest that coach Robert Saleh is hopeful the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL draft will be back for, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com. For now, added WR snaps/targets will be available for Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor alongside Wan'Dale Robinson, with Calvin Ridley also mixing in, an arrangement that was in play during Tennessee's Nov. 1 loss to the Bengals.

In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Patrick suffered a concussion during Sunday's game versus the Rams, and it will keep him out for his third game this season in Week 10. In his absence, rookie sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin figures to take over at center Thursday.

Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not presumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.
